title: How to use conveyor in lightburn
body_html:
How to Use Conveyor in Lightburn

Usage — step-by-step

Step 1 - Set the Parameters

After connecting the Conveyor to the machine's rotary axis port, turn ON the rotary axis switch located next to the port.

In LightBurn, open the Rotary Setup window and configure the following settings:

  • Rotary Type：Select Roller, and check the box to Enable Rotary.
  • Rotary Axis：The default selection is the Y-Axis (some machines may use the A-Axis).
  • Parameters：Input the numerical values found on the aluminum card that came with the unit into the parameter fields on the right side of the pop-up window.

Once configured, the Conveyor is ready to use.

If you encounter a length limitation when processing material with the Conveyor (e.g., restricted to 500 mm):

  • Open Machine Settings in LightBurn.
  • Find Max travel within the U Axis Settings.
  • Change this value to 10000 and Click Write.
  • The Conveyor needs to be turned off and disconnected, then the machine needs to be reset or restarted before the Conveyor can be reconnected to truly write the Max Travel value to the mainboard.

 

Step 2 - Processing Settings

1. We recommend selecting User Origin for Start From and the top left corner for Job Origin. This setting can reduce the occurrence of errors.

2. The width of the graph cannot exceed the working area. Please note that it should not exceed the Max Travel of the X-axis.

 

Step 3 - After Using the Conveyor

In LightBurn, open the Rotary Setup window and uncheck the Enable Rotary box.

Turn OFF the rotary axis switch on the machine and disconnect the Conveyor's cable.

Finally, click the Reset icon on the machine's control panel to restore the machine to its normal processing state.

Caution: 

If the shutdown sequence is incorrect or if you turn off the rotary axis switch directly (skipping the LightBurn disable step), it may cause homing errors or abnormal Y-axis movement.
